why: hasActiveTutorAccess() in firestore.rules grants a tutor read access purely by the existence of a tutor_active_access doc, so its correctness depends on every code path that ends an active grant also deleting that doc. Step 3 (tutor account deleted) does this explicitly. Step 2 (parent account deleted) revokes the same kind of active grant but never deletes the corresponding tutor_active_access doc -- it is orphaned permanently. The underlying data is already gone (Step 1's recursiveDelete), so this is low-blast-radius today, but it's a genuine, silent asymmetry the test suite confirms: the Step-2 test only asserts on grant.state, while the symmetric Step-3 test explicitly asserts the access doc is gone.
recommendation: In Step 2's loop, also delete tutor_active_access/{buildAccessId(grant.tutor_uid, uid, grant.child_profile_id)} for each active grant, mirroring Step 3.
acceptance_criteria: cf_triggers.test.mjs gains a 'W6.23: tutor_active_access doc is deleted when parent grant is revoked' test symmetric to the existing W6.24 one, and it passes.
